title: Pink Halloween Entryway Decor
description: Style a pink Halloween entryway with plain hot-pink pumpkins, black bats, gauze and LED lights, plus optional extras from your own home.
intro: Hot-pink pumpkins and crisp black bats make a small entryway feel ready for Halloween without taking over the whole room. A loose layer of pink gauze and a little LED glow pull the scene together. Keep the console useful, then add a few collected extras from what you already own.

sections.heading: Give the pumpkins one corner
paragraphs: Start with the surface you already have, whether that is a console, a narrow shelf or a small table. Group a few plain hot-pink pumpkins at one end, with the tallest toward the back and smaller shapes in front. The recorded set includes assorted sizes, so check the actual measurements against your tabletop before choosing how many to display.

Leave a clear patch for keys and the everyday things that land by the door. You do not need every pumpkin in the pack on one surface. Black, cream or lavender pieces already in the room can balance the pink without making everything match.

sections.heading: Layer the gauze, then add the glow
paragraphs: Let a gauze panel run under part of the pumpkin group and fall over one edge rather than covering the whole console. Its open weave leaves the surface beneath it visible. Keep any trailing fabric away from handles, the doorway and the walking route.

Loop the pink jack-o-lantern string lights low around the pumpkins, keeping the little black faces visible. If you use a second strand near a mirror, arrange it so the wire and battery pack can sit securely without obstructing the mirror. Check the listing instructions for placement and use.
Tuck the pink LED tea lights into the gaps instead of making an evenly spaced line. Their white plastic flame tips create the candle-like detail; there are no real candle flames in this arrangement.

sections.heading: Let the bats lead your eye upward
paragraphs: A loose rising arc of bats gives the wall a shape to follow. Start near the console and spread the silhouettes farther apart as they travel upward, mixing a few sizes and folding the wings for dimension. A small selection can do the job; the whole pack does not need to go on the wall.

Check that the supplied adhesive suits your wall finish, and follow the product instructions before attaching anything. Keep the bat shapes clear of door hardware and leave room around the mirror so the entry still feels useful.

sections.heading: Borrow the finishing touches
paragraphs: The flowers, mirror, framed artwork, console, chair, blanket basket and silver lantern in the inspiration are styling extras, not part of the five-product shopping list. A frame you already own, a small dish for keys or a few stems in an existing vase can give your version the same collected feeling.

The candy cauldron in the doorway photograph is an optional prop too. Use your own bowl or basket for wrapped treats, and keep the threshold clear. The finished vignette shows how the layers sit together; the porch view shows the entry from a different angle while Tommy Kate answers the open door.
